models_evaluated: simulated logistic regression prediction models (ICU readmission, inpatient falls)

links.outcome: Net monetary benefit of cost-benefit-based cutpoint selection versus Youden and other methods in simulations
links.effect: Value-optimizing cutpoint best in 86% of ICU simulations (median INB $0 vs about -$1412 to -$1478 for ROC-based methods); in falls, cost-based methods comparable (INB ~$15-16) and Youden 3% best.
links.quote: Overall, the threshold which maximized NMB was most commonly the value-optimizing method proposed in this study that considered downstream costs and effects in comparison to other approaches to determining model thresholds.

unlisted_practices: Economic net-monetary-benefit-based cutpoint selection robust to model miscalibration

links.outcome: Net monetary benefit by threshold method
links.effect: Value-optimizing approach was best in 86% of ICU simulations; cost-minimizing was best in 13%.
links.quote: The value-optimizing approach was the best performer in 86% of simulations, whereas the cost-minimizing approach was best in 13% of simulations.

links.outcome: incremental net monetary benefit of cutpoint selection methods
links.effect: Value-optimizing cutpoint was best in 86% of ICU readmission simulations (median INB $0) and 25% of fall simulations (median INB $15.22), frequently outperforming traditional cutpoints like Youden index and closest-to-(0,1).
links.quote: Overall, the threshold which maximized NMB was most commonly the value-optimizing method proposed in this study that considered downstream costs and effects in comparison to other approaches to determining model thresholds.
